root_cause.text: The loop in rose_kill_by_device() uses the wrong index variable (cnt instead of i) when accessing the socket array, causing it to repeatedly dereference the same uninitialized or out-of-bounds array element instead of iterating through collected sockets.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows the fix changing `sk = array[cnt];` to `sk = array[i];` within a for loop that iterates `for (i = 0; i < cnt; i++)`. The variable `cnt` represents the total number of sockets collected (a constant during iteration), while `i` is the loop counter. Using `cnt` as the index means the code always accesses array[cnt], which is either uninitialized (when cnt < ARRAY_SIZE) or out-of-bounds (when cnt == ARRAY_SIZE), leading to invalid socket pointer dereferences and reference leaks from sock_hold().

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix array indexing bug in rose_kill_by_device loop to iterate through all collected sockets instead of repeatedly accessing out-of-bounds memory.
intent_record.what: Changed array indexing from `array[cnt]` to `array[i]` in a loop that iterates from 0 to cnt-1.
intent_record.how: This fixes an out-of-bounds memory access bug. The original code always accessed the same element at index `cnt` (which is beyond the valid range of the array), causing the loop to process the wrong socket repeatedly and potentially access invalid memory. The corrected code properly iterates through each element of the array using the loop variable `i`.

The variable 'cnt' is the loop bound, not the loop iterator, making this a classic off-by-one indexing error.

This causes the loop to dereference the same invalid memory location on every iteration instead of iterating through the collected sockets at indices 0 through cnt-1, directly embodying the root cause of the vulnerability.
